implement.approach: Scanner (single Jest file, TypeScript compiler API, no new deps): (1) walks every .ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx under apps/mobile/src plus App.tsx (excluding tests, .d.ts, __tests__/__mocks__/fixtures); (2) records strings AS RENDERED — a per-file literal resolver maps `const x = '…'` and `OBJ.key` literals so `'…' + '…'` concatenations, `[…].join(sep)`, template literals `${x}` and JSX `{expr}` interpolations are joined before matching; JSX text/attribute entities ( ,  , &#x…) are decoded and invisible code points (soft hyphen, ZW*, LRM/RLM, WJ, BOM, CGJ) stripped; (3) single-word values reach the scan regardless of binding name — implementation tokens are excluded by SHAPE only (identifier-like/camelCase/snake_case/URL/path/hex/kebab tokens, property-name slots, literal type nodes, import/export specifiers), while anything rendered in JSX is always scanned; (4) rules cover Android, Google Play/Play Store/play.google.com, guest-mode phrasings, Live Court(s), DUPR, SwingVision/PB Vision/Selkirk/JOOLA, accuracy % / 'N out of M' correctness claims, an expanded superlative list (best-*, most *, #1, world-class, ultimate, unmatched, top-rated, award-winning, revolutionary, guaranteed results, …) and AI-coach-equivalence phrasings; (5) also scans ios/PickleSensei/Info.plist string values (permission prompts, display name), Swift string literals under apps/mobile/ios (LocalPods + app target), the public /privacy /terms /support text in supabase/functions/api/legal.ts (long template literals reported per paragraph so violations get their own line), and docs/APP_STORE_SUBMISSION.md STORE COPY only — backticked and plain `ENTER:` values, fenced blocks after an ENTER prompt (allowing intervening note lines and list indentation), the character-count table and screenshot captions — so policy prose that names the forbidden terms is not mistaken for submission copy. Each rule has positive fixtures plus approved-copy controls (Confidence 82%, SAVE 33%, 'Rating 7 out of 10', Platform.OS === 'android', provider ids, BillingPlatform union, URLs); the walker has fixtures for concatenation, join, entities, invisible Unicode, single-word bindings, template interpolation, .js/.jsx, and dossier extraction variants. The shipping corpus assertions require non-trivial corpus sizes so an extractor regression cannot pass vacuously. Wiring: the test lives in apps/mobile/__tests__ and runs under the canonical mobile gate (`npx jest --silent` / scripts/verify-cloud.sh), so the audit is on the shipping validation path.

residual_risks: Scanner is regex/AST heuristic, not a language model: copy assembled at runtime from non-literal sources (server responses, i18n tables loaded from JSON, values computed by functions) is not resolved. The resolver follows one level of `const`/object-literal bindings within a file; cross-module imports of copy constants are scanned at their definition site (the defining file is in the walk) but not re-joined at the render site.

Descriptive uses of 'fastest'/'strongest' (e.g. 'the fastest wrist moment in this swing', 'analyzes the strongest swing') are deliberately NOT flagged — they describe a measurement inside a clip, not a product claim. If the reviewer reads the policy as banning every superlative form, those four strings (formReviewModel.ts:918, AnalyzeScreen.tsx:421, GuidedCaptureViewController.swift:409, dossier App Review notes lines 868/875) would need rewording; the Swift one is under the native-pod serial group this package does not hold.
The header comment of apps/mobile/__tests__/paywallPodium.test.tsx still says 'BEST VALUE' (describes the old badge); left unchanged per the hard rule 'do not modify existing code comments'.
The manifest write path 'APP_STORE_SUBMISSION.md' does not exist at the repo root; the authoritative dossier is docs/APP_STORE_SUBMISSION.md and was edited there (listed in out_of_scope_files).

apps/mobile/__tests__/wf/SignInScreen.buttons.test.tsx asserts the UI surfaces a mocked Google Sign-In SDK error 'Google Play services are out of date.' — that text originates from the SDK at runtime, not from app copy, so it is outside the scanner's corpus by design.

Android platform code paths remain in the app (Platform.OS === 'android' checks, BillingPlatform 'android', Android RevenueCat key) as implementation-only; the scan intentionally does not flag them. Removing Android scope is outside this package.
implement.summary: Defect on BASE_SHA: no forbidden-claims scan existed, and the shipping app carried five user-facing violations of docs/APP_STORE_SUBMISSION.md §policy — apps/mobile/src/screens/ManageAccountScreen.tsx:77-78 ('Google Play' / 'Manage subscription in Google Play' in the Android SUBSCRIPTION_MANAGEMENT branch of an iPhone-only app) and :992 (deletion notice '...App Store or Google Play subscription'), apps/mobile/src/screens/PaywallScreen.tsx:572 (hero badge 'BEST VALUE'), apps/mobile/src/screens/AnalyzeScreen.tsx:599 ('...for the most precise read.' — assembled from `+`-concatenated literals, the exact pattern the r1 scanner missed). The r1 scanner had two P1 false-negative classes (concatenation/array-join not joined; single-word terms outside copy-named bindings dropped). Regression test committed first (cdde869c): apps/mobile/__tests__/h06ForbiddenClaims.test.ts, 59 tests — it fails on BASE_SHA naming exactly those five strings and passes on HEAD. Fix commit (104120cf): App Store-only subscription management + deletion notice, 'BEST VALUE' -> 'RECOMMENDED' (two paywall test assertions and the dossier's UPLOAD: screenshot instruction follow), 'the most precise read' -> 'a stroke-specific read'. All three manifest acceptance commands pass, plus the prior-round adversary suite (34/34), pnpm format:check and git diff --check. Branch devin/pp/h06-01/impl-r2 pushed; no PR opened.
